Good Thursday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 626 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Hill's youth wave hits reality
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

Gen Z and millennials launched their biggest bid yet to remake Congress this year. But roughly 7 in 10 were out of contention by early September, Axios' Russell Contreras writes from a new report.

  • Younger generations are struggling to clear the hurdles of a political system that rewards experience, fundraising and established party support.

📈 The report from Future Caucus, a nonpartisan nonprofit that works with younger elected officials, found that a record share of this cycle's congressional candidates came from the country's two youngest political generations.

  • Yet only about 21% of Gen Z congressional candidates remained in the race at the report's September cutoff.
  • That figure rose to 30% for millennials, 41% for Gen Xers and 45% for baby boomers.

Stunning stat: Incumbents averaged 59 years old — nearly nine years older than challengers.

🗳️ Yes, but: Young candidates are scoring some wins.

  • In Colorado, 29-year-old democratic socialist Melat Kiros ousted 15-term Democratic Rep. Diana DeGette in the primary for a heavily Democratic Denver seat.
  • In Iowa, 29-year-old Republican Joe Mitchell, a former state lawmaker, captured his party's nomination for an open House seat.

2. 📺 Trump cancels execution livestream
 
Via Truth Social

President Trump is calling off a livestream of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan's execution by firing squad, Axios' Avery Lotz reports.

  • Trump wrote on Truth Social today: "I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device."
  • "That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose."

🪖 Hasan, a former U.S. Army officer, was convicted of killing 13 people in a 2009 mass shooting.

  • Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said last week that Hasan's death would be livestreamed, drawing bipartisan condemnation.
Chart: Alex Fitzpatrick/Axios. Data: ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos

📊 The vast majority of Americans oppose livestreaming Hasan's execution, per an ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll out this morning.

  • 80% of American adults said the execution should not be livestreamed.
  • Opposition ran higher among Democrats (91% opposed) and independents (83%). But even a majority of Republicans (64%) were against the idea.

Ukrainian firefighters work at the site of a Russian missile strike of an apartment building in Kyiv yesterday. Photo: Genya Savilov/AFP via Getty Images
  1. 🇺🇦 Ukraine's Starlink and Starshield satellite services — critical tools in its war with Russia — have been restored to full capacity, a Ukrainian official tells Axios. The official also said that Ukraine conducted a strike overnight against a Russian oil refinery, defying President Trump's demand that it stop hitting those facilities. More from Barak Ravid.

4. ☀️ 1 for the road: New sunscreen hits shelves
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios

The first sunscreens using bemotrizinol — sometimes called BEMT — are hitting store shelves after the FDA approved them in June.

  • Bemotrizinol has long been the go-to sunscreen option in Europe and elsewhere.

Dermatologists say it offers broad protection but without the downsides of other sunscreens, including white streaking.

  • BEMT has decades of safety data behind it, including studies showing that it has minimal absorption into the skin.
